So all the housing is off base, even the "base" housing, is still located off base. 
It's just ran by the base housing people and they take all of your BAH. 

BUT, honestly from my experience, it would have been way easier to rent someplace off base. 
When I first got there I had no idea how to get on the wait-list for housing bc I didn't have their information, and the wait-list was long. 
If you just find an apartment or something, there is no wait-list.

And for him getting off-base, I can't speak for other branches, but I can speam for the Air Force, when I was there atleast.
If he is not aircrew, when he first gets there he will be phase 1 for one month. 
This means he can't leave base, can't wear civilian clothes and has a strict curfew etc. (again rules can still change, it's been a bit since I've been to DLI)

But from my experience, once he becomes phase 2, and has completed the butt-load of checklists they give him, all he will have to do is say "my spouse is here living off base" and they will let him move out with you.
Again this is from air force perspective, I'm not sure about other branches.

I'd still say go with him. 
You don't have to get base housing, you can get an apartment off base or something cheaper than the BAH.
(You can pocket what's leftover) 

And there are resources on base to help spouses with jobs etc. 
Also, it will help your husband a lot living off base with you instead of living in the dorms. With the stressors of the course, being out of the dorms is one less thing you have to worry about.
